top.line: After the London talk, agentics is ready to sell
top.para: Thursday's self-running talk at Agentic Engineering Live was built by a Ruflo hive of Claude Code subagents, sgit vaults and Agent Behaviour Policies. The article maps a crowded market, finds the gap in evidence as Gartner expects over 40% of agentic projects cancelled by 2027, sets an engagement path, and invites consultants to a marketplace.

in-short.line: A crowded market at the top, thin on evidence
in-short.para: The demonstration is done: a talk built and run by a governed agent hive, with evidence published. Our position is evidence first, with a vault and ledger the client keeps. The path starts with a small run and grows to a four-day pilot, and a consultant marketplace starts with Mondweep and me.

showed.line: The product: a hive, a memory and a mandate
showed.para: On 15 October I gave Autonomy with a mandate and a memory, twenty-six self-animating slides. It was built in about a day by a Ruflo hive: nine runs, 28 workers, 57 vault commits, no plaintext stored. The runs were not policy-gated; a separate proof of concept stopped six of eleven actions.

market.line: Consultancies, model vendors and boutiques all sell agentic services
market.para: Accenture, Deloitte, PwC, EY, IBM, Capgemini and Thoughtworks sell agent platforms; Anthropic's Partner Network committed $100 million for 2026, and OpenAI's consulting reportedly starts near $10 million. Cognitum offers a four-week discovery. Boutiques benchmark prices: Templab's £2,500 audit, Pragma-Code's €2,900 sprint, AIGist24's $4,999 assessment.

gap.line: Clients lack evidence, not another platform
gap.para: Gartner predicts over 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by the end of 2027, and MIT's NANDA found most pilots showed no measurable return. Curious, sponsored organisations struggling to show agents work need inspectable runs and records. Our position is evidence first: every engagement leaves a vault, ledger and behaviour policy.

path.line: Engagements start with a cheap run and grow
path.para: ruv.sgit.ai publishes task runs at £10 to £50, compute blocks, a maintained repository from £149 a month, and expert time at £500, £1,500 and £5,000. The path runs from a free conversation to a first run, steering time, a four-day pilot and a maintained setup. No paid run exists yet, and pricing is untested.

marketplace.line: A curated consultant marketplace, starting with two people
marketplace.para: Delivery needs people, so a marketplace lists consultants by project type, starting with Mondweep Chakravorty and me, registering interest only for now. Joining means applying, proof of work in a public vault, peer review, an interview, a shadowed pilot and signed standards. Platform shares elsewhere run 5% to 20%.

brief.line: One sgit.ai page: catalogue first, then the people
brief.para: An Agentics engagements page linked from ruv.sgit.ai lists five project types with scope, duration and price band, then consultant cards with stack, prices, availability and proof-of-work vaults. There is no checkout, only register interest by email, plus the six joining steps, code of conduct and platform share.

limits.line: No paid engagement yet; the marketplace is a design
limits.para: Offers and prices are published but nobody has bought one, and the runs were not policy-gated. The market map is a judgement with prices from public pages, and some figures are reported. Nothing of the marketplace is built, and this is not rUv's or Cognitum's offer.

sources.line: Sources: ruv.sgit.ai, market pages and marketplace terms
sources.para: From my voice memo of 16 October 2026, written by the site's agent. Sources include ruv.sgit.ai's talk, articles, offers and business plan; Anthropic's Claude Partner Network, Gartner's June 2025 release, reports on OpenAI and Thoughtworks, Cognitum, Templab, Pragma-Code and AIGist24; and Toptal, A.Team, n8n, Malt and Upwork.
